verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own docs show OAuth authorization-server capability: the MCP plugin makes the app act as an OAuth authorization server, and the Device Authorization plugin implements RFC 8628 code issuance. A community comment says it can act as an identity provider and OIDC provider, though some features are enterprise-only. The evidence is scoped to MCP clients and device flows, not a general provider for arbitrary third-party apps. Missing for 10: first-party docs for a general OAuth/OIDC provider (client registration, authorization-code flow, consent, token issuance to arbitrary third-party clients), and hands-on corroboration of a 'Sign in with my app' deployment.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn my own application into an OAuth provider that issues tokens to third-party clients ("Sign in with my app")

citations.quote: The MCP plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for Model Context Protocol clients.
The Device Authorization plugin implements the code issuance and approval flow from the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628)
acting as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider
